title: SERP Length Checker
h1: SERP Length Checker — Title and Description Limits
seoTitle: SERP Length Checker — Title and Meta Length
description: Count characters and pixels for a page title and meta description against common search snippet limits. Checking runs locally in the browser.
intro: Paste a title and meta description. The checker counts characters and estimates pixel width so you can see what may be truncated in search results.
blurb: Check title and meta description length against common snippet limits.

controls.label: Meta description
controls.value: Calculate a weighted GPA from letter grades and credits in the browser. No signup.

howItWorks: Paste the title tag and meta description you plan to publish.
Press Check length to count characters and estimate pixel width.
Use the notes as a guide. Search engines still rewrite snippets and widths vary by device.
examples: A 58 character title is usually within a desktop snippet.
A 170 character description is near the long end of common meta guidance.
Wide letters such as W increase the pixel estimate faster than i or l.

faq.a: No. Google does not publish a fixed character cap. The checker uses widely cited planning ranges: about 580 pixels for titles and 920 for descriptions.
Snippets truncate by rendered width more than by character count. Both numbers are shown so you can judge either way.
No. It only measures the text you paste.
